macro_events.event: Trump Halts Planned Iran Attack — Crude Oil Crashes 5.68%
macro_events.causal_chain: War-risk premium unwinds → crude drops 5.68% to $79.86 → lower input costs for industrials/transports/consumer discretionary → lower inflation expectations → supports broad risk appetite → futures green (S&P +0.40%, Dow +0.56%)
macro_events.second_order: Airlines/cruise lines benefit from lower fuel costs (DAL, UAL, CCL); energy producers face margin pressure (XOM, OXY, BP); gasoline futures decline → consumer spending boost; lower oil reduces headline CPI pressure, potentially easing Fed's hand on September hike
macro_events.analog: Sep 2019 Abqaiq drone attack on Saudi Aramco — oil spiked 15% then fully reversed within 2 weeks as supply fears proved overblown. De-escalation typically plays out even faster.
macro_events.counterargument: Iran situation remains fundamentally unresolved. Any reversal in diplomatic stance → snap-back oil rally and risk-off. Don't over-rotate on a single headline — the Strait of Hormuz chokepoint risk hasn't structurally changed.

macro_events.event: KOSPI Crashes 4% — Samsung & SK Hynix -8%, DRAM ETF -32% on Margin Calls
macro_events.causal_chain: Memory stock overvaluation → margin calls on leveraged Korea/Asia investors → forced selling → KOSPI worst month since 2008 → DRAM ETF collapses 32% → potential contagion to US memory names (MU, WDC)
macro_events.second_order: If margin calls cascade, broad semi ETFs (SMH, SOXX) could see forced selling. However, NVDA and AVGO are AI logic chips — structurally different demand profile from commodity memory. Dip buyers likely step in on quality names. Memory weakness may actually benefit logic chip stocks via capital rotation.
macro_events.analog: Aug 2022 memory downcycle — DRAM oversupply crushed Samsung/Hynix margins for 4 quarters, but NVDA diverged upward on the ChatGPT AI demand pivot. Same structural divergence likely here.
macro_events.counterargument: Global semi sales at $120.6B/month (record, +104% YoY) — this is a leverage/positioning washout, not demand destruction. Charlie Bilello: margin calls in concentrated positions 'almost never end well' — but that's for the leveraged, not the market.

macro_events.causal_chain: Persistent inflation expectations + massive fiscal deficits + AI infrastructure capital demand → structural supply/demand imbalance in Treasuries → term premium expands → 30Y hits 5.19% → higher discount rates pressure long-duration growth stock valuations
macro_events.second_order: Benefits insurers and asset managers with higher portfolio yields (MET, PRU, MKTX, MA); headwind for rate-sensitive sectors (utilities, real estate); mortgage rates rise further; banks' net interest margins expand. El-Erian: 'The sources and uses of funds simply do not align except at higher yields' — AI capex + government deficits = structural bond bear market.
macro_events.analog: 2006-07 yield surge preceded tightening cycle peak. Difference now: AI capital cycle provides genuine growth offset that 2006 housing bubble lacked. Equities can rally with rising yields IF earnings growth outpaces discount rate compression.
macro_events.counterargument: If Friday's NFP comes in soft (+100k expected by Barclays), could catalyze yields lower and spark violent rotation from financials back into growth/tech. The market has been 'climbing the wall of yields' for months.

macro_events.causal_chain: CAT premarket (industrial bellwether for global capex) + BP premarket (energy into crude crash) + SpaceX first earnings → 335 intraday reports → AMD after close (AI GPU demand from hyperscalers) + PLTR after close (AI/government spending)
macro_events.second_order: AMD results set tone for entire AI semiconductor complex tomorrow. Strong AMD guide → NVDA/AVGO/MRVL sympathy rally. Weak → sell-the-news risk amplified by KOSPI memory crash. PLTR consensus: EPS $0.33, revenue $1.81B — government AI contract pipeline is the key variable.
macro_events.analog: Q1 2024 earnings season — AMD and NVDA reports created multi-day momentum moves in either direction. The first mover's guidance sets the narrative for the cohort.
macro_events.counterargument: With 335 reports, individual stock reactions can be swamped by macro. But AMD and PLTR are consensus-critical names — their after-hours moves will dominate tomorrow's premarket.

macro_events.event: FedWatch: 64.5% Probability of September Rate Hike
macro_events.causal_chain: Fed held at July FOMC but Warsh signaled willingness to defend 2% inflation target → market pricing 64.5% odds of another hike → 2Y at 4.25%, 10Y at 4.69% → stronger dollar (DXY 99.81) → EM and commodity headwind
macro_events.second_order: Gold resilient at $4,055 despite hawkish Fed suggests structural real-asset demand from central banks; BTC -1.62% as opportunity cost of zero-yield assets rises; USD strength pressures multinational earnings translations
macro_events.analog: 2018 tightening cycle — Fed hiked into strength while market rallied, until the December pivot. Key difference: AI capex cycle is genuinely productive investment, not financial engineering.
macro_events.counterargument: Market has been pricing hikes and rallying anyway — equity risk premium compression is the dominant force. Unless NFP massively surprises, September hike is largely priced in.
